stories.title: Transactional persistence
stories.implementation: Build the first Workspace persistence vertical slice: StateStore/EventStore/BlobStore ports, WorkspaceService create and policy-update commands, bounded rusqlite writer, versioned schema migration/fingerprint, encrypted content-addressed filesystem blobs through an injected WorkspaceBlobKeyProvider, atomic aggregate/event/origin-sequence commit, restart and projection replay. The desktop OS key-provider implementation exists; platform qualification, rotation/recovery tests, and cryptographic review remain open. SQLite v3 adds/backfills RuntimeWorkspaceBinding and gates Attempt admission. New CODE coverage migrates a v2 database with active and revoked Runtime records, injects failure during the v4 table rebuild after v3 commits, verifies the binding projection and retry boundary, and retries through the current schema without changing authorization roles/status. Current daemon source persists installation-scoped identity and has local Runtime Workspace-binding enrollment/query; packaged/OS key-provider qualification remains open. BlobStore negative tests transplant valid ciphertext across Workspace/purpose scopes and prove AAD authentication rejects it; deletion tests prove missing-object idempotency and rejection of symlink/directory objects without touching the symlink target. The adapter checks the configured root and each Workspace/purpose directory, rejecting static symlink redirection for put/get/remove; purpose-symlink tests verify outside sentinels remain unchanged. Reopen tests reject changed migration source checksums, and reads with a missing scoped key fail closed. Directory-handle protection against concurrent same-user replacement races is not claimed. `cargo test --locked -p storage-sqlite` passes 144 tests including these checks. V4 removes the legacy Runtime-to-single-Workspace ownership column and four composite foreign keys; multi-Workspace authorization still requires role-scoped active RuntimeWorkspaceBinding checks in admission and readiness. rusqlite remains provisional pending SP02 comparison. Deterministic writer saturation CODE now gates the production writer, fills the bounded queue with a real Workspace commit after an abandoned read reply, enqueues Shutdown, verifies Full on the next send, then reopens and confirms commit/event replay: `cargo test --locked -p storage-sqlite` passed 174 tests and strict package Clippy passed on Linux WSL2 x86_64 (Rust/Cargo 1.98.1). This proves finite graceful queue drain and abandoned reply delivery, not caller cancellation support, sustained capacity, memory, or physical disk exhaustion. A separate actor-level SQLite `max_page_count` test submits a real Workspace commit, observes `SQLITE_FULL`, proves the original projection/event sequence/replay remain intact, restores capacity through the writer, retries the exact revision at origin sequence 2, and verifies replay; `cargo test --locked -p storage-sqlite` passed 175 tests and strict package Clippy on Linux WSL2 x86_64 (Rust/Cargo 1.98.1). A service-level `SQLITE_FULL` test now fills available SQLite pages using valid idempotent `WorkspaceService` policy changes, verifies the failed request has no receipt and leaves projection/event/sequence/replay unchanged, then retries that exact request and confirms receipt replay creates no duplicate event; the cap does not prove which SQL statement first hit `SQLITE_FULL`, and aggregate blobs may be left unreferenced until temp cleanup. `cargo test --locked -p storage-sqlite` passed 177 tests and strict package Clippy passed on Linux WSL2 x86_64 (Rust/Cargo 1.98.1). These tests do not qualify physical disk/WAL/blob exhaustion, OS key-provider behavior, or owner acceptance. A direct transaction-level `BeforeCommit` regression now supplies a request receipt, proves Workspace/event/origin-sequence/receipt rollback after the receipt INSERT, then verifies exact retry and replay; `cargo test --locked -p storage-sqlite` passed 189 tests and strict package Clippy passed on Linux WSL2 x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Rust/Cargo 1.98.1. See `implementation/reviews/E01-S02.md` and `implementation/CURRENT-RUN.md`. Current-HEAD CODE coverage also reopens the on-disk adapter after a committed Workspace policy request, replays the original receipt with the stale expected version, and rejects changed-payload reuse without another event or receipt: `workspace_policy_receipt_replays_after_store_reopen`. `cargo test --locked -p storage-sqlite` passed 191 tests and strict package Clippy/rustfmt passed on Linux WSL2 x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Rust/Cargo 1.98.1 (SQLite 3.53.2). This is additional CODE evidence with no production behavior change; physical database/WAL/blob exhaustion, live OS key stores, platform/SYSTEM evidence, cryptographic review and owner acceptance remain pending.
stories.acceptance: On-disk SQLite and filesystem adapters commit Workspace state/event/sequence atomically; one of two stale competing writes wins; restart replay equals the current projection; migration/configuration drift, unsupported schema, missing keys and blob authentication fail closed. Owner acceptance remains pending and E01-S01 is still IN_REVIEW.
stories.negative_cases: Concurrent stale writes; injected rollback after aggregate, sequence and event writes; busy timeout; interrupted migration/retry; schema fingerprint drift; corrupt ciphertext; wrong Workspace or purpose; broad blob directory permissions; failed blob commit; missing-object deletion idempotency; rejection of symlink/non-regular blob objects; and rejection of symlinked BlobStore root or Workspace/purpose directory ancestors. SQLite `max_page_count` now exercises `SQLITE_FULL` through the production writer actor and verifies retry continuity. A valid idempotent WorkspaceService path additionally proves failed-command projection/event/sequence/receipt rollback, exact retry, and receipt replay; it does not identify which transaction statement first encountered `SQLITE_FULL`. Physical database/WAL/blob-filesystem exhaustion and production key-provider cases remain untested.

stories.title: Independent Runtime lifecycle
stories.implementation: Partial: litecoworkd run/status acquires a cross-process single-instance file lock, persists local bootstrap Runtime/incarnation identity and lifecycle state atomically, opens LocalWorkspaceStorage, serves authenticated local Operator routes, reports DEGRADED until Task recovery/execution exists, and closes storage on shutdown. If Operator initialization fails after incarnation registration, the catalog is already DEGRADED; the specific OPERATOR_API_START_FAILED blocker is stored in private local status and the daemon exits nonzero to release the lock for bounded supervisor/manual retry. A spawned real daemon SYSTEM probe in a private temporary directory confirmed that unavailable Secret Service credentials produce a persisted DEGRADED Runtime/NOT_RUNNING status and exit before IPC admission. The user systemd default target is active, but the credential service is unavailable and this shell has no delegated writable cgroup path; successful daemon lifecycle, cgroup scope, and provider qualification remain open. Current CODE evidence is recorded in implementation/reviews/E01-S03.md: shutdown settlement and IPC deadlines, durable Runtime transition/fencing, managed systemd unit filesystem tests, startup failure/recovery blockers, authenticated SQLite lifecycle projection, child-process lock exclusion plus killed-process unclean-incarnation recovery, and SQLite tests proving a superseded incarnation cannot acquire or renew an active ExecutionLease. The lease fixture does not replace full StepAttemptStore admission. `cargo test --locked -p litecoworkd` passes 134 unit plus 4 CLI tests, and `cargo test --locked -p storage-sqlite` passes 146 tests; strict package Clippy passes. Remaining: full domain recovery, authenticated start/stop controls, native service-manager qualification, sleep/wake, dependency-aware drain preview, and process identity reconciliation. Live successful systemd/package behavior, platform qualification, and owner acceptance remain unverified. New integrated CODE test connects private `RuntimeLocalState::begin` and the production Runtime registration helper to real SQLite: it proves unclean restart state persists on the new current incarnation and stale lease insert/renew triggers reject without changing the old lease. The focused integration, killed-owner lock, storage stale-lease checks, full daemon suite (134 unit + 4 CLI), and strict daemon Clippy passed on Linux WSL2 x86_64 with Rust/Cargo 1.98.1. Fixed test key/device identity and an FK-disabled fixture seed do not qualify OS identity providers, StepAttemptStore, full daemon restart, service managers, or owner USER acceptance. See `implementation/reviews/E01-S03.md`. Latest guarded startup-recovery CODE evidence calls the production recovery helper against a real SQLite store with a complete historical execution graph, enabled foreign keys/triggers, four durable settlement events, and an idempotent repeat; focused and full daemon tests, strict Clippy, rustfmt, and diff checks pass. This does not spawn the full daemon/Operator path, admit a new Attempt, prove process quiescence, or reconcile Effects. See implementation/reviews/E01-S03.md. Additional Linux process-scope cleanup CODE evidence (2026-10-12): linux-process-scope tests cover gate timeout/invalid marker and READY/GO_CONSUMED stripping, plus injected direct-child reap failure through fail_scope retaining PendingCleanup and succeeding on retry; failed systemd kill and cgroup disappearance also retain retryable cleanup ownership. Package tests pass (14 passed, 6 live systemd/Bubblewrap tests ignored) and strict Clippy passes. Environment validation now precedes cgroup/systemd side effects; empty PATH is rejected without a systemd request. Live membership/limit checks, Attempt admission integration, real systemd/cgroup qualification, and owner USER acceptance remain open. An injected `Command::spawn` error now returns the original failure after a successful slice stop or retains an exact `AttemptSlice` stop-only retry handle when cleanup fails. Started-slice parent validation failure also retains exact cleanup ownership when stop fails; retries require positive unit/cgroup quiescence proof and preserve ownership across repeated stop failures. Focused/full crate tests, strict Clippy, and Windows fail-closed API compilation are recorded in `implementation/reviews/E01-S03.md`. Latest hardening also retains exact-slice ownership when systemd reports an ambiguous start error and allows retry settlement only after independent positive unit/cgroup quiescence evidence; the full package suite passes 19 tests. Startup recovery transaction failure CODE evidence now uses the production pre-Operator recovery/blocker helper and a real SQLite trigger to prove lease/Attempt/Step/Task state and recovery events roll back atomically; the private DEGRADED blocker is persisted before Operator initialization, then retry succeeds after removing the fault. Focused test, full daemon suite (138 unit + 4 CLI), strict Clippy, rustfmt, and architecture/coverage/plan validators pass. See implementation/reviews/E01-S03.md; spawned-daemon/provider, OS, and USER gates remain open.
stories.acceptance: Closing Operator leaves daemon running; reboot changes incarnation; stale process cannot own a lease; workers lazy-start.
stories.negative_cases: Duplicate startup, SIGKILL/restart, corrupted/symlinked state, lock-file symlink/broad permissions, sleep during write, invalid state directory permissions, storage/key-store recovery failure, and shutdown signal during drain.
stories.demo: Start the daemon twice against one state directory, inspect DEGRADED status, stop gracefully, restart and inspect incarnation/recovery state. This demonstrates bootstrap lifecycle only; Task recovery and authenticated control remain pending.

stories.title: Authenticated Operator boundary
stories.implementation: Partial local integration: litecoworkd dispatches existing Axum handlers through authenticated Unix IPC on Linux/macOS and source-integrated Windows named pipes. Runtime-to-OS-principal binding, bounded framing, readiness checks, Workspace-owner authorization, and the Tauri native client remain on the shared path. Windows uses an isolated TokenLogonSid adapter, protected current-logon-SID/SYSTEM DACL, remote-client rejection, and keyed Runtime binding; the daemon dispatches both transports through common bounded request workers. Windows security/IPC crates cross-compile and pass helper tests. Full daemon Windows Rust cfg `cargo check` and Clippy pass with host SQLite pkg-config metadata, but Windows SQLite linking and Tauri source cross-compilation remain unverified (MinGW GCC and windres are absent), as does Windows host qualification. The former bearer/loopback descriptor path is removed. Recent CODE slices include owner-scoped GET /resources/{resourceId}/locations with one Workspace/Resource-scoped SQLite projection, committed-only freshness, stable ordering, empty/missing/cross-Workspace behavior, and omission of provider/private locator references; the IPC adapter also preserves the required X-Resource-Revision-Id response header through an explicit finite allowlist. The pure UI reducer enforces the stream schema's minimum projection version, Workspace-bound resync reason, and closed top-level fields on stream.ready, stream.resync_required, turn.delta, and rich.draft plus event-specific rich-draft payload keys. It rejects a malformed item across a complete projection snapshot/update without advancing the cursor; focused tests pass 19/19, though fixtures are not validated against the JSON Schema and there is no production projection adapter. The current UI suite/build evidence is recorded in implementation/reviews/E01-S04.md. The Artifact UI wire types now derive from generated OpenAPI schema/operation types; the UI build enforces generator freshness and retains native-only IPC transport. The Resource detail editor also reads committed location observations through a finite Tauri command, with a closed public-field decoder and Workspace/Resource-fenced UI state. New direct IPC codec evidence covers unsafe IDs/paths/headers, length/version/correlation guards, partial-header timeouts, progress-refreshed body deadlines and body-budget release: operator-ipc passes 12 unit plus 2 Unix endpoint integration tests, and the daemon IPC suite passes 6/6, including stable Idempotency-Key replay across different frame correlation IDs and changed-payload conflict. The production Workspace-create route, strict decoder, idempotency-key parser, and commit seam are exercised through authenticated Unix IPC with a real SQLite store: a fresh frame correlation ID replays the original body/correlation for the same stable key and payload; changed payload under that key conflicts without a second commit. The Tauri bridge tests pass 2/2, the location API/state tests pass 6/6, the full Tauri Rust suite passes 32/32, the full UI helper suite passes 106/106, and the pinned Node production build passes. A frozen-lockfile install was blocked by pnpm's existing ignored esbuild build-script policy, without changing that policy. This is not yet a complete generated service client. The storage layer now provides a bounded, one-Workspace/one-origin replay page over durable origin_sequence values, with same-read head/floor, explicit gap/ahead results, a 500-entry cap, metadata-only rows, and an integrity failure when the allocator head trails a persisted event; focused storage tests and the full storage suite pass (144 tests). The Conversation presentation read includes its durable origin_sequence frontier from the same SQLite transaction. RichPresentationStore also exposes a bounded 20-filter batch read: SQLite authorizes once and reads every projection and message frontier from the same transaction; the existing singular read delegates to it. The deterministic two-Conversation writer race test proves replay recovers a commit made after that common frontier. The storage CODE evidence now supports an Operator route for one to 20 filters; the desktop consumer remains scoped to one selected Conversation. Multi-filter reconnect, corruption, retention-race, packaged, and owner USER qualification remain open. A barrier-controlled storage test now pauses after capturing that frontier, commits a message plus matching event from an independent connection, proves the snapshot remains pre-commit, then proves bounded event replay and a projection read after the snapshot message frontier recover the committed records. The existing authenticated Unix stream integration separately covers production dispatcher refresh/reconnect behavior. An initial authenticated local conversation_presentation stream now binds a one-Conversation filter and opaque cursor, emits ready/snapshot/resync frames, polls bounded metadata-only replay pages, refreshes the authorized snapshot after Workspace events, enforces two sessions/1 MiB writes/five-second deadlines, cancels on daemon shutdown, and monitors the client request side between response frames so idle EOF/reset releases stream admission while post-subscription bytes are rejected. A real SQLite plus same-UID Unix socket test covers handshake, snapshot, committed-event refresh, idle disconnect, stream-slot reuse, and shutdown EOF; operator-ipc, JSON Schema, and reducer tests pass. Task presentation snapshot streaming and its desktop consumer now have CODE evidence for same-read Task/Plan/Artifact frontier, full-interval replay-gap detection, owner-authorized snapshot refresh, reconnect catch-up, foreign-Task cursor resync, atomic UI replacement, and stale/reconnecting state while resync is pending. The Runtime-inventory invalidation stream now emits closed bounded notifications over authenticated local IPC, rechecks Workspace owner/active EXECUTOR authorization, binds cursors to the Runtime incarnation, resyncs malformed cursors, and rereads profiles on notifications and offer expiry. The focused Runtime inventory CODE regression now traverses the authenticated same-UID Unix IPC dispatcher and verifies handshake, authorized change invalidations, locator redaction, disconnect cleanup, invalid-cursor resync, initial Workspace denial, midstream owner-revocation closure, and stream-slot reuse; the full daemon suite, strict daemon Clippy, architecture/coverage/plan validators pass. The full Workspace Runtime-binding inventory is now owner-scoped and paged through an authenticated Operator route backed by one bounded SQLite query; it includes retained PENDING/ACTIVE/REVOKED records in binary binding-ID order with Workspace/page-size-bound cursors. Focused storage and same-UID Unix IPC route tests, full storage/daemon package tests, workspace strict Clippy, architecture/coverage/plan validators, and generated OpenAPI UI build pass. This is partial CODE evidence only; packaged and owner USER gates remain open. Other UI cursor/resync/privacy checks, scheduled expiry refresh logic, and the JSON-safe revision boundary remain covered. Remaining: broader event replay/reconnect semantics, packaged desktop slow-consumer/reconnect behavior, production OS and packaged SYSTEM qualification, and owner USER acceptance. One spawned-daemon CODE test now verifies exact Workspace-create replay after a clean process restart; other route, stream, OS, and packaged restart cases remain unqualified. The deterministic Conversation snapshot/writer race CODE case also passes. The Tauri Conversation stream consumer now has CODE coverage for selected-session fencing, accepted-cursor reconnect, page-preserving snapshot merge, native subscribe/cancel transport, and no-idle-timeout session frame reads; a route-level exhausted-admission test returns `429 CAPACITY_EXCEEDED`. The native-to-WebView path now grants one frame at a time: session-scoped frame IDs are acknowledged only after UI reduction/discard, stale/duplicate/foreign acknowledgements are rejected, cancellation drops a pending wait, and a five-second acknowledgement deadline closes stalled streams. Tauri tests cover the pending-slot guard and timeout/cancellation; a stalled IPC writer test proves cancellation releases the shared frame budget. These are CODE checks and do not prove packaged runtime behavior. The tested command idempotency replay is a separate mutation behavior. E01-S04 remains incomplete: full OS and packaged desktop qualification, remaining routes, complete event replay/reconnect semantics and packaged slow-consumer behavior, complete generated service client, lifecycle controls, adversarial identity tests, and owner USER acceptance. The latest multi-filter route run passes the full daemon suite (115 unit and 4 CLI tests), strict Clippy across `operator-ipc`, `storage-sqlite`, and `litecoworkd`, and the real Unix IPC reconnect/filter-mismatch/owner-revocation integration. The `operator-ipc` package passes 19 unit and 3 endpoint integration tests; the full SQLite package passes 144 tests. Architecture validation, regenerated coverage, implementation-plan validation, and five stream contract tests pass. An earlier shared `scripts/check.sh` also passed workspace checks; packaged desktop behavior and the remaining SYSTEM/USER gates are still open. See docs/LOCAL-OPERATOR-IPC.md and implementation/reviews/E01-S04.md. Do not treat CODE evidence as story completion. The Runtime capability-host inventory now has CODE evidence for a Workspace-owner and active EXECUTOR-scoped SQLite read, current-incarnation cursor fencing, bounded pagination, Workspace-scoped active-use counts, stale-health projection, and provider-reference omission; focused storage and same-UID Unix IPC tests, full storage/daemon suites, strict Clippy, generated OpenAPI UI build, and architecture/coverage/plan validators pass. Packaged, cross-identity, Windows/macOS, restart/replay, remaining-route, and owner USER gates remain open. The Conversation stream catch-up paths now revalidate the durable Workspace/origin event page after lazy subscription admission and before cursor advance. A deterministic retained-row loss regression proves resync marker, replacement snapshot, and missed-message recovery; full daemon tests, focused replay tests, strict Clippy, and stream contract tests pass. This remains CODE evidence; packaged/platform and USER gates are open. Multi-Conversation retained-history resync now retains the last message included in each bounded replacement snapshot and continues catch-up when another page exists; focused two-Conversation cursor test, SQLite-backed multi-filter retained-gap route test, full daemon suite (136 unit + 4 CLI), and strict Clippy pass. Existing multi-Conversation route fixture directly inserts projection messages and removes a Workspace event; it is not an atomic message/DomainEvent commit or production retention worker. Task stream replay now confirms the durable Workspace/origin page after the authorized snapshot and before cursor advance. Its deterministic production-route test removes sequence 5 after the first replay read, commits sequence 6 after the sequence-5 snapshot and before confirmation, and verifies the stale snapshot is withheld before a gap marker and replacement snapshot at sequence 6. This fixture does not model a production retention worker. The focused Task stream regression, full daemon suite (136 unit + 4 CLI), strict daemon Clippy, and targeted rustfmt pass. CODE only; packaged/platform/restart and owner USER gates remain open. A real Unix socket lifecycle regression also queues malformed bytes from a peer, verifies the listener captures credentials then rejects before returning a frame-capable connection, observes peer closure, and accepts a subsequent authorized peer. `cargo test --locked -p operator-ipc` passed 19 unit + 4 lifecycle tests and strict Clippy; the focused daemon IPC suite passed 23 tests. This same-UID callback denial does not qualify a different UID or platform, packaged operation, or owner acceptance; see `implementation/reviews/E01-S04.md`. The existing dependency invalidation history OpenAPI route is now implemented through an owner- and exact-edge-scoped SQLite read and authenticated Operator route, with stable bounded pagination, Workspace/edge/page-size-bound cursors, nondisclosing missing-edge behavior, a closed response projection, and no-store responses. Storage and real SQLite route CODE tests cover continuation, empty history, owner denial, cursor binding, and response fields; package suites, strict Clippy, and repository architecture/plan/coverage validators pass. Producer, packaged, cross-identity, and USER gates remain open. The authenticated GET /resources/{resourceId}/dependents CODE slice now checks ArtifactVersion and VerificationRun authoritative pinned inputs, derives freshness from revision heads, and has focused plus full storage/daemon test evidence; packaged/platform and USER gates remain open. The Task stream reconnect integration also closes/reopens SQLite and rebinds authenticated IPC under a new route incarnation, proving the accepted pre-outage cursor yields the durable sequence-4 snapshot before a sequence-5 live update; focused and full daemon suites and strict Clippy pass. This remains same-process route/store reinitialization, not packaged daemon process restart or SYSTEM evidence. A spawned-daemon CODE test also saves a Task presentation cursor, commits a Task revision while disconnected, restarts against the same SQLite state, verifies authorized snapshot catch-up and a live post-restart projection. It uses test-only identity/blob-key providers and graceful SIGTERM; packaged/systemd, production keyring, open-stream EOF, abrupt-crash, cross-OS, and USER evidence remain pending.

stories.title: Desktop shell/onboarding
stories.implementation: Partial: Tauri 2 + React shell has Home/Work/Library/Needs You/Settings, honest empty states, and native Runtime lifecycle commands. Settings lists and creates Workspaces through the authenticated local Operator API and blocks creation until a successful authenticated Workspace-list read; its create controls remain disabled during list loading/failure, then recover after retry. Home blocks its Task composer and recent-work list until a Workspace is selected; first-run checks the authenticated Workspace list, distinguishes loading/error and Runtime offline/reconnecting/degraded/unavailable states, and reuses the same create command. Workspace create uses a synchronous submit guard, retains the original Idempotency-Key and name after ambiguous failure, prevents stale list responses from erasing a committed Workspace, and fences late success from overriding a newer Workspace selection. Runtime refresh clears stale readiness while status is checked and after a failed check, and Workspace creation is guarded on authenticated readiness. Focused Home helper tests pass 5/5, the full UI suite passes 210/210 including six daemon-sidecar packaging tests, and rendered Chrome checks 26/26, including production App list/create and Runtime refresh races over mocked Tauri IPC; Node 24/pnpm 12.10.1 API/typecheck/Vite build passes (810.26 kB minified JS / 224.16 kB gzip). Earlier responsive-shell, Node guard, frozen-install, and Tauri workspace evidence is recorded in implementation/reviews/E02-S01.md. stories.title: Workspace policy and instructions
stories.implementation: Partial source: authenticated Workspace replication-policy update has expected-version checks, idempotent transaction receipts, and a desktop Settings selector; a real-SQLite authenticated route regression verifies exact replay, changed-payload and changed-If-Match conflicts, same-owner cross-Workspace key-reuse conflict, stale-version conflict, non-owner denial, and mismatched Workspace path/header denial; immutable instruction revisions use pinned same-Workspace UTF-8 text Resources, transactional local projection/event/receipt writes, opaque paginated history, and a desktop editor/history view. The first desktop instruction save accepts the contract-required empty parent list, and the Tauri policy allowlist uses ACTIVE_TASK_INPUTS while rejecting the misspelled ACTIVE_TASKS and keeps SELECTED_FOLDERS unavailable in the local V1 UI. The backend domain service now requires a non-empty unique root-ID list, sorts IDs deterministically, and delegates active same-Workspace validation to the serialized SQLite transaction; real-SQLite regressions cover active roots, exact replay after version advance, paused/unknown-root rejection, and no partial commit. Folder transfer remains disabled by V1 scope (implementation/reviews/E02-S02.md). Storage's first-revision parent check, pre-receipt Workspace version check, stale conflict ordering, and commit-time Resource-head check were corrected. New instruction revisions require a current Resource head at commit; existing immutable pins remain valid after Resource advancement. Real-SQLite WorkspaceService regressions commit revisions 1 and 2, verify ordered history and exact replay after Workspace advancement, reject changed-payload request-key reuse, prove stale writes leave no partial state, and prove an injected event failure rolls back. Authenticated Operator route regressions verify history rejects a mismatched path/header Workspace ID and a non-owner without disclosing Workspace state; another route integration test creates revisions 1 and 2, retries revision 1 after both Workspace and Resource advancement, walks the opaque history cursor in order, and rejects that cursor on another Workspace through real SQLite and the encrypted local BlobStore. A bounded-content route test rejects mismatched digest, non-text media, invalid UTF-8, historical/non-current Resource revisions, and >64 KiB Resource content without any instruction writes. Task creation copies the current instruction revision into its initial TaskSpec and storage validates it against the Workspace; a real-SQLite authenticated route regression creates instruction revision 1 through the production route, creates a Task through the production handler, advances instructions to revision 2 through the route, and verifies the persisted Task remains pinned to revision 1. The Settings editor now keeps per-Workspace unsaved drafts, fences late content/history responses, preserves exact retry IDs and concurrency pins, discloses Resource-import/commit partial outcomes, and separates confirmed commit status from refresh failures. Seven focused helper tests and a mocked-bridge browser interaction check cover these frontend states; the full UI helper suite and production build pass. Authenticated route tests now reject foreign Workspace scope, cross-Workspace Resource IDs, missing Resources/revisions, and null/omitted unpinned revisions without instruction writes; direct SQLite tests reject foreign/missing/unpinned refs without partial state. Existing tests also reject historical heads, bad digests/media/UTF-8/size. The Settings editor has per-Workspace draft recovery, exact retry IDs, disclosed partial Resource imports, stale comparison and committed/refresh-pending states, covered by helper tests and mocked-bridge browser checks. Verified Linux CODE slice: four real filesystem tests now cover no-follow WorkspaceRoot selection, traversal/root and final/intermediate-symlink rejection, selected-path replacement, and held-identity revalidation; the test exposed and fixed canonicalization-before-no-follow. The full litecoworkd suite (128 unit + 4 CLI), strict Clippy, and rustfmt pass. SQLite now atomically rejects a duplicate non-revoked FOLDER identity in the same Workspace under a different RequestId while exact replay returns its original receipt; real-SQLite coverage verifies no Resource/location/private-binding/root/event/receipt rows are added. The WorkspaceRoot overlap CODE slice now rejects equal or ancestor/descendant canonical paths within a Workspace under the serialized create transaction; exact request replay still wins first, and ACTIVE/PAUSED/UNAVAILABLE roots reserve scope until REVOKED. Fourteen focused real-SQLite tests cover both insertion orders, real temporary directories, prefix siblings, paused/unavailable/revoked scope, identical paths across separate Workspaces, malformed/noncanonical/oversized locators, two-writer races, and rollback at every SQL projection/event/receipt boundary. Encrypted aggregate blobs are written before the transaction and can remain as unreferenced immutable objects after SQL failure; safe reference-fenced blob reclamation remains open. Archive has an owner-scoped Tauri/Operator/SQLite route and Settings confirmation; transactional checks cover persisted workloads, authority, unresolved Effects, pending Approvals, active channel hosts and persisted AutomationCursors, with safe typed blockers. Eight SQLite plus two daemon route regressions and all 53 Tauri tests pass; the browser interaction remains mocked. The encrypted v7 lexical projection stores encrypted text snapshots and Workspace/purpose-scoped HMAC tokens, matches deterministic Unicode terms with AND, returns bounded snippets with revision provenance, and fails closed if the key is unavailable. Initial plans require a current active TASK_PLANNING session; replan admission remains unavailable until Attempt/lease authority exists. The Home composer saves standalone Tasks with exact pinned Resource revisions, server-resolved Coworker revision/failover provenance, and a same-window retry envelope that retains the original RequestId and lead/Coworker snapshot; changed drafts are blocked until the owner checks Work and explicitly clears the unresolved retry. Tauri validates returned Task/TaskSpec identity, objective, and ordered Resource refs, and the UI independently checks the returned objective and inputs before clearing the draft. The retry envelope is not persisted across application restart. The composer does not admit planning or execution. The API plan POST remains unwired because authenticated Operator requests do not yet carry trusted producer-scoped session authority; no native agent invokes the plan service. Task detail has a read-only planning-readiness diagnostic through the authenticated GET route; it shows sanitized blockers and always reports planning dispatch unavailable. It creates no execution state and remains source-only/unverified. See F100 and F106. Source is unbuilt/untested and this story does not meet acceptance.

stories.title: Adaptive Artifact Workbench and version history
stories.implementation: Partial: Artifact Workbench exposes a native Save As action for the exact selected managed ArtifactVersion up to 10 MiB. Its registered Tauri command checks expected Artifact/Workspace/version, ResourceRevision, digest, media type and size; the authenticated daemon content route verifies stored bytes and the native bridge checks response media/length before a same-directory staged write. Cancel does not read content; only Saved/Cancelled returns through WebView IPC. It also exposes an on-demand list of the latest 10 immutable versions through the existing authenticated exact-version read route, bounded text editing through the mounted append route, and a managed text/plain restore-as-new-version draft. Restore requires explicit confirmation and separate publication against a freshly loaded current head; stale conflicts preserve the draft. The append contract records user.text_edit but does not persist a distinct restored_from relation. An unconfirmed text-version publish locks the in-memory draft and original RequestId, disables edit/discard/close, and offers unchanged retry; it is not restart-persistent. Adjacent managed text versions can be opened by exact version metadata/content routes and compared side-by-side with the same bounded safe renderer; each pane labels its exact ResourceRevision. The comparison is read-only and does not identify changed lines or publish content. Recent history exposes exact output revision plus source-count/provider/Attempt provenance when recorded. Full qualified renderers, external/non-text restore, Library provenance, renderer sandboxing, and owner/system/code acceptance remain open. Current source has not been built or verified. Managed Markdown preview also supports a bounded safe subset (headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes, fenced code, inline emphasis/code, confirmed HTTPS links) using React text nodes; unsupported or malformed syntax falls back to source text and no remote images load. This is not full CommonMark or an editor. Source remains unbuilt/unverified.
stories.acceptance: No immutable version is overwritten; conflicts are recoverable; restore appends a new ArtifactVersion; renderer failure preserves download/provenance; revoked sources are not represented as currently authorized context.
stories.negative_cases: Concurrent edits, stale compare input, restore racing a new version, linked/external or non-plain-text restore request, text over 1 MiB, missing historical blob, unchanged-content restore, incompatible renderer, hostile document, revoked source while open, dirty close/navigation; native Save As cancel without content fetch, selected-version/ResourceRevision/digest/media/size mismatch, external or >10 MiB content, daemon digest rejection, response media/length mismatch, temporary-write/rename failure preserving the destination, and no bytes/full path crossing WebView IPC.
stories.demo: Review a generated document/spreadsheet and coding diff; compare, save the exact selected version to a chosen path, edit, resolve a version conflict, restore a prior version as a new version, restart, and inspect provenance.

stories.title: Semantic-first RichPresentation and Host Guidance
stories.implementation: Commit semantic ConversationMessage and settle its turn without waiting for optional rich compilation. Add immutable RichPresentation publication/read paths, closed schema validation, bounded model intent, exact semantic/Artifact/Resource/source bindings, deterministic tool/result renderers, safe fallback, and Conversation-only negotiated HostSkill guidance. Keep host-bound system blocks sourced only from Core projections. Add bounded retry-fenced rich draft transport only after semantic streaming is stable. This story does not add arbitrary React plugins, side chats, cloud sync, or remote Runtime behavior.
stories.acceptance: Simple answers use no extra model call; complete semantic text is visible before any enhancement. Rich content is independently immutable/digest-bound and optional. Unsupported adapters still work. No model-generated status/approval/verification/download authority is rendered. Missing/invalid blobs, schema, renderer, or stream frames preserve semantic history. Exact ArtifactVersion deliverables and owner-requested deterministic ZIP work with digest-verified downloads. Rich UI passes accessibility, reduced-motion, responsive, and local-only desktop qualification.
stories.negative_cases: Hostile/invalid intent; forged host-bound block; cross-Workspace Resource/Artifact ref; message digest mismatch; missing/corrupt blob; unsupported renderer/version; stale retry frame; stream overflow/gap; direct media URL; unsafe Markdown/Mermaid/URL; bundle path traversal/duplicate path; missing source version; reduced-motion and high-zoom failures.
stories.demo: Run plain and rich Conversation requests with a qualified native Agent; disconnect during semantic and rich streaming; force compiler and blob failures; produce a Task report with exact Artifact cards and a reproducible ZIP; show semantic fallback, screen-reader/reduced-motion states, and direct-native comparison timing.
